name: jira-versions
label: Jira versions
description: Lets Copilot chats add and remove Jira fix versions with `jira-versions …`, which acli can't, through Atlassian's MCP server and your own login. Each change asks you first.

JIRA_MCP_SITE.label: Jira site (optional)
JIRA_MCP_SITE.hint: Your site's address, like acme.atlassian.net. Empty: the Jira site Clearsky already uses (JIRA_URL, or the one acli is logged in to).

JIRA_MCP_URL.label: MCP server (advanced)
JIRA_MCP_URL.hint: Atlassian's remote MCP server. Leave empty for https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp.
JIRA_MCP_URL.patternHint: the address should start with https://

JIRA_MCP_SCOPES.label: Scopes (advanced)
JIRA_MCP_SCOPES.hint: Jira read and write scopes if empty.Space-separated scopes asked for at login. If empty, Clearsky asks for the scopes the server lists that read or write Jira work, plus staying logged in: no Confluence, nothing for admins. The door itself only reads a ticket and writes its fix versions.

secrets.note: your Atlassian login for the MCP server (and the client it registered), in ~/.config/clearsky/jira-versions-mcp.json

doors.name: jira-versions
doors.about: adds and removes a ticket's fix versions as you, after you OK each change; nothing else in Jira

note: Reaches Atlassian's MCP server with your login. Only reads tickets and writes their fix versions; every change asks you in the chat first and is in Copilot's changes.
outside: It changes Jira with your login for chats that can't hold it, which is what a door is for.
